name: Spitzkoppe: Rock Arch to Bushman's Paradise
region: Spitzkoppe, Erongo, between Usakos and Swakopmund
why: Sand tracks between red granite domes, from the stone arch that frames the Spitzkoppe to a chain up a bare slab into a hidden green valley with San rock paintings.
book: Pay the entrance fee at the Spitzkoppe community rest camp reception, about 50 km from Usakos (B2, then gravel D1918 and D3716). The rock-art sites, Bushman's Paradise included, are visited only with a local guide from the reception (tip). Arrange a car to pick you up at the end.
water: No water on the way and no running water at most camp pitches: carry 2-3 litres each.
dangers: Heat: over 35 °C from October to March, little shade. Walk in the early morning.
The slab to Bushman's Paradise is steep and polished: hold the chain, and stay off it when wet.
Loose sand and sharp granite: closed shoes, and watch for snakes and scorpions under rocks.
turnaround: Not at the foot of the Bushman's Paradise slab by 10:30 in hot weather: get picked up and come back early next morning.

points.name: Spitzkoppe Rock Arch
points.note: A granite arch on the south side of the Pontok domes, with the Spitzkoppe framed in it. Best at first light.

points.name: Foot of the Bushman's Paradise slab
points.note: At the end of the sand track on the east side of the Pontok mountains. A fixed chain runs up the bare granite slab.

points.name: Bushman's Paradise
points.note: A green basin among the domes and an overhang with San paintings, 2,000-4,000 years old, many of them damaged. Back down the chain.
